title: Saying no: the alternative, the cost and the date

videos.script: A request arrives on a Thursday. A festival wants group bookings before its next season, and the head of product asks whether Checkout can fit them in. About ninety hours, it sounds small. {{request}} Saying yes feels free, because the hours look like nobody's. They are somebody's. A team of six has three hundred and sixty focus hours in a sprint, and every one of them was already promised to something. Ninety of them is a quarter of the sprint. {{capacity}} Lesson eight of the architect communication course taught you how to say no well. This lesson adds what a strategy brings to that conversation. An alternative that fits the guiding policy. The cost, in hours and in what the strategy loses. And a date when the answer can change. {{three}} Then comes the most useful answer of all, which is not yet. Not yet is honest only when it carries a condition somebody else can check. {{condition}} By the end of this lesson you can turn a request into a decision, with the numbers in front of the person who has the authority to make it. {{decision}}
